objective: Determine whether the existing solver-fed BreakingLipMesh can depict a coherent open hydraulic crest and falling plunge without changing water, collision, buoyancy, or raft-physics authority.

v161_open_plunge_lip_only.decision: rejected: the elongated open profile reads as a broad translucent rectangular card rather than an overturning sheet

v164_surface_only_control.decision: diagnostic control: hiding the lip and both particle systems removes the broad patch, localizing the artifact to BreakingLipMesh

v165_transparent_carrier_lace.decision: rejected: suppressing the translucent carrier removes the card but leaves the hydraulic nearly invisible

v167_masked_cutout_threshold.decision: rejected: the masked two-sided variant renders as an opaque beige faceted slab and is materially worse than the translucent fallback

restoration.restored_baseline: validated v160 attached moderate arch, strong-jump curl blend, sparse translucent lace, and bounded v121 nested-shell fallback

decision: Do not retain the open-plunge geometry or masked-material approach. BreakingLipMesh cannot produce the required coherent live hydraulic with the tested connected-sheet materials. Preserve the v160 technical baseline and its isolation diagnostics, but reject all v161-v167 imagery for M9 acceptance. M9 remains open and no milestone commit or push is permitted.
